summary: Angela Manderscheid works in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa under Nalini Devdas. In 2008, she was attested as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities.

Angela Zito, a scholar of religious studies and sinology, earned her Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1980–1989). Around 2000, she became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University, an institution she founded.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs studied at Freiburg, Oxford, Konstanz, Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt, earning her PhD under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt (1993–2001), and the University of Basel (2001), holding the Lehrstuhl für Praktische Philosophie.

Angelika Malinar works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Mainz and Tübingen (PhD and Habilitation), she taught at the Free University of Berlin (~1999–2000) and SOAS (~2000–2007), becoming extraordinary professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.

Indologist and linguist Angelo de Gubernatis studied at Turin and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Florence (1863–1891) and professor of Sanskrit and Italian literature at Rome (1890).

Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (Ph.D.). He founded Sandhaan in 1988 and served as its director (attested 1999).

Ankur Barua, active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and The University of Hong Kong. He held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Master of Arts degree at the Australian National University (attested 1983) under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy degree at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1971–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

Ann Heirman specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012), where she became a professor of Chinese language and culture and head of Buddhist studies (~2000).

Ann Laura Stoler works in history and archaeology. Educated at Barnard College and Columbia University, she taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and the University of Michigan (1989–2004), becoming chair of anthropology at The New School in 2004.

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg University and completed an MA at the University of Tübingen (1998). She served as assistant professor to the Chair of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, completed her PhD at SOAS under Lionel Caplan and studied under Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became research coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anna Brown, active in religious studies, was attested in 2017 as a Zen student of Robert Kennedy. In 2017, she was attested as chair of political science and director of the social justice program at Saint Peter's University.

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields is a scholar in the field of sinology. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and at Princeton University (~2015).

Anna Madelyn Hennessey specializes in sinology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2011) under the doctoral supervision of William F. Powell.

Anna Morpurgo Davies was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1955–1959). She subsequently held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1962 to 2004.
